chunks: Ali ibn Ja'far narrated from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) who said:

I asked him about a man who married a woman but did not consummate the marriage with her, and then he committed fornication; what is upon him? He said: 'He is lashed with the flogging penalty, his head is shaved, he is separated from his family, and he is exiled for one year.'

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: consummated the marriage (entered into sexual relations)
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ الْحَدَّ: he is lashed with the prescribed flogging penalty

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a man who commits fornication before consummating his marriage?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim, the distinction is made between the punishment for a non-married man (rajm) and a married man (jild) by specifying that even without consummation, the marriage contract suffices to incur the flogging (hadd) and additional disciplinary measures like head-shaving and exile. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the legal status of 'muhsan' (married) applies upon the valid contract, not merely physical intimacy, thereby triggering the specific hadd penalties for fornication.
